mode.title: Mode
mode.description: supervised asks a person at both approvals (the specs, the sign-off). auto decides them by rules when it is safe and says so in Slack, and asks a person otherwise. Only the exact word auto is auto.

def.description: Read the ticket from GitHub.
Read the GitHub issue and its first comments.
Turn the GitHub issue into one plain ticket (key, title, description).
Name the change (kebab-case, built only from [a-z0-9-]) and its change and archive folders.
Read openspec/ on the base branch - capabilities, exact requirement names, active changes and project rules (openspec-format skill).
Write the change - proposal, delta specs, tasks and optional design - and, when the repository has no openspec/ folder, its skeleton (openspec-format and delta-specs skills).
Validate the change the way `openspec validate --strict` does and against the requirement names the scan read.
Review a change that passes the check; give a failing one one fix round.
The first proposal passed the check.
Write the change again from a clean checkout, using the first attempt's files as a draft and fixing what the check reported (one round).

def.description: Build only when the join found an approved decision. specs_decision also reads spec_change, which runs whatever the approval said, so a rejected approval still reaches the join and this gate stops the run.

Build the tasks in order, one test per scenario, tick them when done (implement-from-specs skill). The worker runs the repository's own tests after it submits and sends failures back; a repository with no test command that can be found counts as failed.
Check the code against every requirement and scenario - completeness, correctness, coherence (spec-verify skill, advisory).

Push only an archive the check accepts.
What is wrong with the archive.

Commit the change, with the merged specs and the archived folder, onto the commit the work was cut from and push it as an azhi/ branch (Git Data API).

def.description: Review the pull request with pr-review (reviewers, a verifier, a summarizer) and post the review on it. Only the commits after the pushed base are reviewed, so a stacked pull request is not reviewed twice. It never offers to merge.
Read the review - approved, findings to fix, or unavailable when the child failed or its verdict cannot be read.
Sign off an approved review, fix the confirmed findings once, and send back a review nobody can read.
The review approved the pull request; no fix round is needed.
Fix the findings the review confirmed, once, on top of the archived change (fix-findings command). The findings are data. The worker runs the repository's tests after it submits.
Push the fix only when the repository's tests pass on it.
Push the fixed change to the same branch, onto the same base commit (the branch's single commit is replaced, so the files are the whole change).
